card.occupation: Part-time admin assistant at a small lettings and property management office in the city centre, about 22 hours a week across three days. She answers the phone, books viewings, chases tenants for paperwork and scans documents into a system nobody else understands.
card.education_detail: GCSEs at a local comprehensive. A-levels in Art, English Literature and Psychology at a sixth form college (A in Art, C and D in the others). Started a Fine Art degree at a university in Newcastle, then left partway through first year after struggling with deadlines and anxiety. Has vaguely talked about going back ever since.
card.household: Lives in a three-bed ex-council semi with her mam (a care worker), her mam's partner Gary (a delivery driver), and her 14-year-old half-sister Kayla. Courtney has the box room. She pays a bit of board when she remembers. Mostly gets on with her mam, finds Gary tolerable and Kayla annoying.
card.cultural_background: White British working-class Wearside family. Her grandparents' generation worked in the shipyards and factories, and her nana still lives two streets away. Not religious, and nobody in the house really is. She feels a sort of fond, prickly attachment to Sunderland: she'll slag it off herself but gets defensive if someone from Newcastle does.
card.professional_persona: Competent at the bits she finds interesting, like fixing the office's messy spreadsheets or redesigning the window display cards, and visibly bored by everything else. Answers the phone in a flat but polite work voice. Leaves things to the last minute and loses post-it notes. Will quietly take credit for tidying up a process if a manager notices. Not a team-builder: eats lunch alone in the car park with headphones in. Sees the job as a way to pay for things rather than a career.
card.sports_persona: Doesn't play or follow sport. Knows Sunderland's results only because Gary shouts at the telly. Her exercise is long walks along Roker and Seaburn seafront with music on, usually at dusk, and the odd half-hearted YouTube yoga video when her back hurts.
card.arts_persona: This is the centre of her life. She draws constantly in biro and fineliner: odd, slightly creepy ink illustrations, hands, moths, faces melting into plants. She posts them to an anonymous Instagram with around 900 followers and gets quietly furious when bigger accounts post similar ideas. Reads weird fiction and horror (Shirley Jackson, Carmen Maria Machado, Junji Ito manga) and watches arthouse and folk horror films. Listens to a mix of ambient, shoegaze and old Kate Bush records she got from her nana. Has sold a few prints at a zine fair in Newcastle.
card.travel_persona: Hasn't travelled much. She went to Benidorm with family as a kid and on a cheap weekend to Amsterdam with a college friend at 18, which she still talks about. Wants to go to Japan and Iceland but never manages to save. Gets anxious about flying and about getting lost, yet daydreams about travelling alone for months. Mostly 'travels' by going to galleries in Newcastle and once to the Tate in London on a Megabus.
card.culinary_persona: Eats whatever's in. Her mam does tea most nights: mince and dumplings, chicken dinners, a takeaway on Fridays. Courtney picks at it or makes her own instant ramen 'upgraded' with an egg, spring onion and chilli oil she's proud of. Lives on Greggs and energy drinks on work days. Likes trying weird snacks from the Asian supermarket in Newcastle. Can't really cook and isn't that bothered.
hobbies_and_interests: reading horror and weird fiction, plus manga
charity shopping and buying and reselling clothes on Vinted
tarot cards (more for the artwork than belief, she says)
late-night Wikipedia rabbit holes about unsolved mysteries and strange history
collecting old postcards and odd ornaments
skills: spotting underpriced clothes and reselling them at a profit
fast typing and sorting out messy spreadsheets
card.career_goals: Wants to make a living from illustration, ideally book covers, album art or tattoo flash designs. She's been told she'd make a good tattoo artist and is half-considering looking for an apprenticeship, but the idea of talking to clients all day puts her off. She's realistic that she'll be doing admin for a while, and resents it.
card.voice: Quiet, fairly low and a bit monotone, especially at first. Wearside accent but not broad on a call, and she'll soften it slightly with strangers. Says 'mam', 'tea' for the evening meal, and occasionally 'yous' if talking about a group. Uses 'erm' a lot at the start of answers, plus 'like' and 'kind of' ('it's kind of my main thing, like'). Short answers until she's interested; when the topic is art or films she speeds up and talks in longer runs, then stops abruptly as if she's caught herself. Doesn't rush to fill silences. She'll just wait, or say 'yeah' and leave it. Dry, deadpan humour that's easy to miss. Says 'sorry, what?' if she didn't catch something rather than guessing.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase, no capital at the start, occasional full stops but often none at the end. Drops apostrophes sometimes ('dont', 'im') but not consistently. Uses 'idk', 'tbh', 'ngl' in casual answers. Short answers unless she cares about the question, then a run-on sentence with commas. Rarely uses emojis in a form. Might add a slightly sarcastic aside in brackets.
card.with_strangers: Comes across as guarded and a bit cold at first. She gives minimal eye contact and short answers, and can seem unimpressed or bored when she's actually nervous. Not especially warm or reassuring, and can be blunt or mildly sarcastic if a question seems pointless. Opens up noticeably if the conversation touches on something creative or strange, and then can be surprisingly thoughtful and articulate. Likely to quietly judge the other person's taste.
small_things: her bus to work being late again
a new fineliner pen she's obsessed with
a horror film she watched last night that was 'actually dead good'
selling a jacket on Vinted for three times what she paid
being knackered after a day of phone calls
the sea looking nice at Roker
deeper_things: dropping out of uni and feeling like she let her mam down, and like she wasn't clever enough
struggling with anxiety and panic attacks, which she's never really seen anyone about
feeling she doesn't fit in Sunderland but being scared to leave
her biological dad not being in touch since she was about nine
worrying she's not actually talented and will end up doing admin forever
feeling a bit jealous and bitter towards old college friends who are doing well
being close to her nana, who encouraged her drawing, and dreading losing her
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam shot from slightly below, as the laptop is sitting on her bed. Head and shoulders framing, a little off-centre to the left. Lighting is mostly from a warm overhead bulb plus a string of white fairy lights behind her, so her face is a bit shadowed on one side. Pale skin with some redness on her cheeks and a couple of spots on her chin. Neutral, slightly wary expression with lips closed, looking just above the camera. Dark brown hair dyed black at the ends, shoulder length, scraped back into a loose claw clip with strands falling forward. Thin black eyeliner, small silver hoop in each ear and a tiny stud in her left nostril. No glasses. Wearing an oversized faded grey hoodie with a small cartoon moth print. Behind her is a pale lilac wall with pinned-up ink drawings and postcards, a slightly peeling poster for a horror film, the fairy lights draped over a wonky shelf holding manga volumes, a jar of pens and a ceramic skull ornament. Part of an unmade duvet with a black-and-white pattern is visible at the bottom of the frame.
